relevance_note: Single-family case report describing three affected relatives with a heterozygous TNFAIP3 VUS: 'The proband, his daughter, and his sister who are all affected with chronic urticaria and angioedema each carry the c.65G>A (p.R22Q) variant inTNFAIP3'; the authors do not diagnose HA20.
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; no table exists and no script transcribed data (a script only assembled the JSON and checked spans). Labels: the index case has no paper identifier, so rule 5 gives 'patient'; relatives follow rule 2 ('sister of patient', 'daughter of patient', 'mother of patient'). Scope: four people. The mother is in scope as a tested-negative relative (TNFAIP3 negative; GJB2 c.35del heterozygous), so she has a GJB2 row but no TNFAIP3 row. The father ('the proband's father was deceased') was neither tested nor described as affected and gets no row; other sisters implied by 'one of the proband's sisters' and the pedigree (Figure 1, not available as text) get no rows. Variants: the paper prints the TNFAIP3 variant once in full (Chr6(GRCh38) g., NM_001270507.1 c., p.(Arg22Gln)) and elsewhere as 'c.65G>A (p.R22Q)'; relatives' rows use the sentence tying them to the variant plus the full description. GJB2 is printed 'c.35del' in Results and 'c.35delG' in the Conclusion (same variant, notation difference). Zygosity of the proband's GJB2 variant and inheritance of all variants are not stated, so left 'not reported' (the daughter's father is the carrier proband, but the paper does not state inheritance). Functional evidence: only in silico prediction and molecular modelling (Monte Carlo/electrostatics) are reported, and the authors say functional analyses are still needed, so functional_evidence_statement is 'not reported'. Possible inconsistencies: Methods say reads were aligned to GRCh37/hg19 while variant coordinates are labelled GRCh38; the Introduction and 'Limitations' say WES found no other disease-associated/causative variants, yet Results report a pathogenic GJB2 variant possibly linked to the proband's mild hearing loss. Judgement calls: 'anti-IgE receptor antibody was elevated' recorded as checklist 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' observed; 'CBC with differential within normal limits' recorded as 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' excluded; urticaria/hives recorded as checklist skin lesions observed; the mother's 'unaffected' recorded as excluded chronic urticaria and angioedema (narrow), leaving the broad skin-lesions checklist item not reported. Normal TSH was not used to exclude autoimmune thyroiditis; diarrhea was not used for GI inflammation; dizziness was not used for CNS involvement.
